scope.description: Three-release deepening tranche for the Pokemon Card Fan Club GET point prize ladder: 500 GET Eevee row 160, 600 GET Shining Magikarp row 235, and 700 GET Porygon row 161. The tranche emphasizes point-bank participation, campaign-logo / rarity-symbol boundaries, Japanese name handling, illustrator separation, and route traps against JR, League, Neo, Awakening Legends, Cool Porygon, Gift Pack, and ordinary Base memories.

context.name_en: Pokemon Card Fan Club 500 GET point prize

main_chase_cards.name: Eevee
main_chase_cards.why: Eevee is the soft entry point into the GET ladder: not just a beloved character, but a record of a fan slowly accumulating 500 points inside the club.

key_artists.name: Toshinao Aoki
key_artists.why: Aoki's Japanese Fan Club Eevee is the important split from Kagemaru Himeno's English Wizards / JR-related Eevee memory.

claims.text: The local source slice models one Pokemon Card Fan Club 500 GET point prize row: Eevee row 160.
Bulbapedia says the Japanese Fan Club Eevee print was available through the Pokemon Card Fan Club from April 2000 until the end of December 2002 and required 500 GET Points.
Bulbapedia credits the Japanese Fan Club Eevee print to Toshinao Aoki, while the later English Wizards Promo route uses a separate Kagemaru Himeno credit.

The 500 GET Eevee sits in the same broader Eevee memory field as Wizards Promo 11 and JR East gold-course Eevee, but its assembly route is the Fan Club point bank, not a rail-rally or English Wizards release.
This row matters because the Pokemon Card Fan Club turned ordinary affection into a ledger: an Eevee could be earned by sustained participation, not pulled from a pack.

Agents should preserve Fan Club 500 GET route, row 160 identity, Japanese name イーブイ / Eievui, Toshinao Aoki Japanese print credit, and non-equivalence with JR East gold-course Eevee, English Wizards Promo 11, Pokemon League Eevee, Jungle Eevee, and later Eevee memories before accepting a match.

narrative.human_title: Fan Club 500 GET — Eevee as earned affection
narrative.why_it_matters: The 500 GET Eevee is charming because it makes fandom measurable without making it cold. Someone did not just open a booster and hope. They stayed in the club long enough for the ledger to hand back an Eevee. That is why the card needs a route-aware instruction: it looks like a familiar Eevee memory, but its identity is the Fan Club point bank, the Aoki Japanese print, and the little social machine around GET points.

context.name_en: Pokemon Card Fan Club 600 GET point prize

main_chase_cards.name: Shining Magikarp
main_chase_cards.why: Shining Magikarp is the ladder's strange jewel: a famous secret-style Pokemon whose Fan Club copy is earned through 600 GET points and lacks a rarity symbol.

key_artists.name: Ken Sugimori
key_artists.why: Sugimori's Shining Magikarp makes the weakest old joke of a Pokemon into one of the franchise's best route-sensitive prize objects.

claims.text: The local source slice models one Pokemon Card Fan Club 600 GET point prize row: Shining Magikarp row 235.
Bulbapedia says the Fan Club Shining Magikarp print was available through the Pokemon Card Fan Club from May 2001 until the end of December 2002 and required 600 GET Points.
Bulbapedia notes that the Fan Club Shining Magikarp print lacks a rarity symbol and has the same embossed foil treatment later featured on Shining Pokemon from Neo Revelation.
Bulbapedia credits Shining Magikarp to Ken Sugimori.
This row is load-bearing for agents because it combines three strong memories that can be accidentally collapsed: Fan Club redemption, Shining Pokemon texture, and no-rarity-symbol appearance.

Agents should preserve Fan Club 600 GET route, row 235 identity, Japanese name ひかるコイキング / Hikaru Koiking, Ken Sugimori credit, rarity-symbol absence, and non-equivalence with Awakening Legends, Neo Revelation, English Neo Revelation, and Shining Gyarados memories before accepting a match.

narrative.human_title: Fan Club 600 GET — Shining Magikarp before the shortcut
narrative.why_it_matters: This is the ladder's card that most needs the new instruction field. A Shining Magikarp with no rarity symbol will tempt an agent to say too much too fast. The honest version is better: 600 GET Fan Club redemption, row 235, Ken Sugimori, rarity-symbol absence, and embossed Shining texture all assemble the card, but none of that proves a seller's physical copy without evidence.

narrative.human_title: Shining Magikarp — the 600 GET prize that can fool an eager agent
narrative.why_it_matters: Shining Magikarp is already one of Pokemon's best jokes: weakness polished into treasure. The Fan Club prize adds another layer. It lacks a rarity symbol, has Shining texture, and belongs to a point-redemption path. An agent should love that, but slowly. The route is the difference between useful catalog memory and an overconfident match.

context.name_en: Pokemon Card Fan Club 700 GET point prize

main_chase_cards.name: Porygon
main_chase_cards.why: Porygon is the ladder's strange endpoint: the artificial Pokemon, credited to Tomoaki Imakuni, carrying the Fan Club GET campaign logo instead of an ordinary expansion mark.

key_artists.name: Tomoaki Imakuni
key_artists.why: Imakuni's Porygon credit makes the artificial Pokemon feel like a media-performance object, which fits the Fan Club reward path beautifully.

claims.text: The local source slice models one Pokemon Card Fan Club 700 GET point prize row: Porygon row 161.
Bulbapedia says the Fan Club Porygon print was available through the Pokemon Card Fan Club from April 2000 until the end of December 2002 and required 700 GET Points.
Bulbapedia says the Fan Club Porygon card features the Pokemon Card Fan Club GET campaign logo in place of an expansion symbol.
Bulbapedia credits the Fan Club Porygon print to Tomoaki Imakuni.
The 700 GET Porygon is the ladder's weird conceptual capstone: a digital Pokemon, an Imakuni credit, and a campaign logo all make the card feel assembled by the fan system around it.

Agents should preserve Fan Club 700 GET route, row 161 identity, Japanese name ポリゴン / Porygon, Tomoaki Imakuni credit, GET campaign logo in place of expansion symbol, and non-equivalence with Cool Porygon, Base/Gift Pack Porygon, Expansion Sheet Porygon, and later Porygon memories before accepting a match.

narrative.human_title: Fan Club 700 GET — Porygon as the ladder's strange machine
narrative.why_it_matters: Porygon is already an artificial Pokemon, a little polygonal thought experiment sitting inside the franchise. The Fan Club 700 GET prize makes that feeling even sharper: a card earned through a point system, marked by a GET campaign logo, and credited to Tomoaki Imakuni. It is not just a Porygon. It is Porygon as a club-machine artifact.
